design.design:
A. SHAPE
- Drugs reuse Procurement's document tables (PO, GRN, indent), state machines, GST maths and numbering, through a domain column ('stores' or 'pharmacy').
- They do so through new connection-taking core functions with domain guards, so a stores route can never touch a pharmacy document.
- Helix remains the only owner of drug stock. One new service, pharmacy_stock_service, is the only writer of helix_inventory_lots and helix_stock_movements.
- inventory_items.is_pharmacy CHECK (is_pharmacy = 0) stays. No drug ever enters inventory_items or stock_movements, so each physical drug has exactly one ledger.

B. SWITCHES (all default OFF)
- config._module_opt_in(env) sits beside _module_enabled. It is ON only for 1, true, on or yes, the same idiom as config.py:866-867.
  - ORB_PHARMACY_STORE: the module (routes, tab, new Helix transition fields).
  - ORB_PHARMACY_WARD_STOCK: ward imprest and crash-cart stores may be created. A site turns it on only after GRN-RS5.
  - ORB_PHARMACY_NDPS_REGISTER: the register hook. It refuses to turn on, logs an ERROR and stays off, unless ORB_PHARMACY_NDPS_ON_FAILURE is set to 'block' or 'record', which is the outcome of GRN-RS7. Both modes are built; neither is chosen by this design.
  - ORB_PHARMACY_NEAR_EXPIRY_DAYS, default 90.
- 'pharmacy-store' is registered in HOSPITAL_MODULE_ENV and enabled_modules(), so /api/health publishes it.
- Client: OPT_IN_MODULE_IDS = ['pharmacy-store'], and DEFAULT_MODULE_FLAGS[id] = !OPT_IN_MODULE_IDS.includes(id). A failed health fetch keeps the defaults, so an opt-in module never appears because of a network blip.
- The stock predicates are data-driven and never read the flag. Turning the flag off after use therefore cannot make quarantined, in-transit or ward stock dispensable.
- Always-on changes, stated honestly. grn-1 and grn-3 are additive schema. grn-4 makes the dispense run in an immediate transaction, with a relative decrement and an in-transaction clinical_access audit row. Screens and behaviour (1 unit, FEFO, in date) are identical for legacy lots (store NULL, status 'available').

C. DATA MODEL
Two migrations, numbered at merge after 47.

M-a helix_tables_in_runner (grn-1)
- A FROZEN copy of today's six Helix CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements and four indexes, never an import of HELIX_SCHEMA.
- Run one statement per conn.execute, as migration 44 does. executescript would commit the runner's transaction.
- init_helix_db stays as an idempotent fallback.

M-b pharmacy_store_schema (grn-3)
Additive only: ALTER ADD COLUMN, new tables, indexes and triggers. No rebuilds and no new foreign keys.

RULE 1. NO CHECK ON COLUMNS ADDED TO HELIX TABLES
- helix_medication_master and helix_inventory_lots are FK parents and can never be rebuilt in a migration.
- helix_stock_movements is a child, but a ledger rebuild is costly, and its type list will grow (op_sale, consumption).
- Their enums are therefore validated in pharmacy_stock_service and pharmacy_master_service against constants: LOT_STATUSES, MOVEMENT_TYPES, DRUG_SCHEDULES, NDPS_CATEGORIES, STORAGE_CONDITIONS, IDENTITY_STATUSES.
- A test pins each set, and reconcile() reports any stored value outside it.
- CHECKs are used only on new pharmacy_* and ndps_* tables and on columns added to the migration-20 tables, which have no FK children.

RULE 2. NAMING THAT THE RESEED SWEEP CANNOT MISREAD
- Never add a column named order_id, medication_id, admission_id, or <procurement table stem>_id without a declared FK.
- Patient-order links use helix_order_id and helix_medication_id.
- Links to procurement documents use the _ref suffix: receipt_line_ref, source_indent_ref, source_indent_line_ref, helix_lot_ref.
- test_reseed_orphans asserts the intended wipe or keep membership of every new table by name.

helix_medication_master (new columns)
- pack_size_units, purchase_uom, dispense_unit, hsn_code, manufacturer.
- gst_rate_bp: NULL means 'Not configured'.
- drug_schedule (none|G|H|H1|X|NULL); ndps_category (none|narcotic|psychotropic|NULL). NULL means unclassified and is never read as none.
- is_essential_narcotic INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.
- storage_condition, reorder_level_units, reorder_qty_units, lead_time_days.
- is_active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.
- identity_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' (draft|active|retired).
- updated_by, updated_at.

helix_inventory_lots (new columns)
- store_id INTEGER. NULL means legacy, before adoption by the dispensing store.
- status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'available' (available|quarantined|recalled|nsq|pending_inspection|written_off|returned_to_vendor).
- units_per_pack, mrp_pack_paise, unit_cost_paise, mfg_date, vendor_id, receipt_line_ref.
- received_at; created_at, which is nullable because ALTER cannot default to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP. The service always sets it.
- Indexes:
  - (medication_id, store_id, status, expiration_date);
  - partial UNIQUE (medication_id, store_id, lot_number, expiration_date) WHERE store_id IS NOT NULL.

helix_stock_movements (new columns)
- movement_type, store_id, balance_after_units, unit_cost_paise, reference_type, reference_id, actor_id, remarks.
- idempotency_key, with a partial UNIQUE index.
- occurred_at: canonical UTC from clinical_time.
- seq INTEGER, with a partial UNIQUE index. It is allocated as MAX(seq)+1 under the write lock and is the ledger's ordering key, because rowid on this TEXT-PK table can change on VACUUM.
- Index on (medication_id, store_id, seq).

Columns added to migration-20 tables (CHECKs allowed)
- purchase_orders, goods_receipts, indents: domain TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'stores' CHECK (stores|pharmacy).
- indents: indent_kind (purchase|issue) and issuing_store_id.
- purchase_order_lines, goods_receipt_lines, indent_lines: helix_medication_id and units_per_pack.
- goods_receipt_lines: free_quantity_milli NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, mrp_pack_paise, mfg_date, helix_lot_ref.
- indent_lines: issued_quantity_milli NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.
- vendors: drug_licence_numbers, drug_licence_valid_to, ndps_licence_number.
- stores: pharmacy_kind CHECK (NULL|dispensing|sub_store|ndps_vault|returns_quarantine|ward_imprest|crash_cart), with a partial UNIQUE index on pharmacy_kind WHERE pharmacy_kind='dispensing' AND is_active=1.

New tables (no FKs)
- pharmacy_par_levels (master, kept on reseed).
- pharmacy_transfers: transfer_number, from_store_id, to_store_id, source_indent_ref, status CHECK, dispatched_by/at, received_by/at, cancel_reason, idempotency_key UNIQUE.
- pharmacy_transfer_lines: source_indent_line_ref, helix_medication_id, from_lot_id, to_lot_id, batch_no, expiry_date, quantity_units, received_units, discrepancy_reason.
- pharmacy_lot_events: append-only by service.
- pharmacy_stock_counts and pharmacy_stock_count_lines.
- pharmacy_ward_returns: carries patient_id and helix_order_id.
- pharmacy_vendor_returns and pharmacy_vendor_return_lines.
- pharmacy_master_change_requests: helix_medication_id, change_kind CHECK (classification_downgrade|identity_create|identity_correction|retire), field, from_value, to_value, reason, requested_by/at, decided_by/at, decision CHECK (pending|approved|refused|withdrawn). A master, kept on reseed.
- ndps_variances.
- ndps_register:
  - columns: store_id, helix_medication_id, lot_id, batch_no, entry_type CHECK, signed quantity_units, balance_after_units, counterparty_type, counterparty_ref, patient_id, helix_order_id, document_ref, actor_id, witness_id, seq, occurred_at, remarks;
  - lane TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (live|non_production), written from config.DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE ('prod' means live);
  - trg_ndps_register_no_update RAISE(ABORT);
  - trg_ndps_register_no_delete RAISE(ABORT) WHEN OLD.lane <> 'non_production'.

Reseed wiring (in grn-3)
- EXTRA_TABLES_TO_CLEAR gains pharmacy_transfers, pharmacy_transfer_lines, pharmacy_lot_events, pharmacy_stock_counts, pharmacy_stock_count_lines, pharmacy_vendor_returns, pharmacy_vendor_return_lines and ndps_variances.
- pharmacy_ward_returns is wiped by its patient_id.
- _CONDITIONAL_DELETE_PREDICATES gains ndps_register: "lane = 'non_production'". A dev reseed clears dev register rows; a prod register can never be deleted.
- Kept: helix_inventory_lots and helix_medication_master (the existing pins still hold), pharmacy_par_levels and pharmacy_master_change_requests.

Document series rows: PHPO, PHGRN, PHIND, PHTRF, PHVR, PHRET, PHCNT, each with is_configured=0.

Backfill
- occurred_at = clinical_time.to_utc_iso(timestamp, naive_tz=UTC), because CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is naive UTC.
- Legacy 'dispense' rows get movement_type 'dispense', reference_type 'helix_order' and reference_id = order_id.
- For each lot whose quantity differs from SUM(quantity_change), write one 'opening' row:
  - quantity = quantity minus the sum;
  - dated 1 second before that lot's earliest movement, or at migration time when it has none;
  - remark "Balance brought forward when the stock ledger began".
- seq: opening rows first, then legacy rows by (occurred_at, rowid). balance_after is the running sum per lot, so no running balance is negative.
- Then lot quantity = SUM(ledger) holds everywhere.

D. SERVICES

services/pharmacy_stock_service.py (grn-4): the only writer of drug stock
- site_today(): moved from helix_service._expiry_cutoff, which now delegates to it.
- dispensable_lot_sql(): one predicate used by dispense, pre-flight, Formulary, reorder and reports:
  - quantity > 0;
  - date(expiration_date) >= site_today;
  - status = 'available';
  - and a location condition: store_id IS NULL (legacy), OR the store is the active 'dispensing' store, OR the store is an active 'ndps_vault' AND the drug's ndps_category is narcotic or psychotropic.
- pick_fefo_lot(conn, medication_id, units, lot_id=None) and dispensable_units(conn, medication_id).
- post_movement(conn, ...):
  - asserts conn.in_transaction and validates movement_type;
  - UPDATE quantity = quantity + ? WHERE id = ? AND quantity + ? >= 0, refusing when no row changes;
  - allocates seq, writes balance_after, idempotency_key, actor and occurred_at;
  - calls the NDPS hook, a no-op until grn-13 and the switch.
- open_or_merge_lot(conn, ...); set_lot_status(conn, ...), which writes pharmacy_lot_events.
- adopt_legacy_lots(conn, dispensing_store_id, actor): assigns NULL lots. Duplicate legacy lots (same drug, batch and expiry) are merged by paired transfer_out and transfer_in movements, never by deleting a row.
- receive_grn_lines(conn, ...); reconcile(conn).
- It never opens a db_session. Callers own one immediate session, so the module is safe under ORB_DB_POOL=0.
- An AST test enforces the single-writer rule:
  - it covers INSERT INTO, UPDATE and DELETE FROM on helix_inventory_lots and helix_stock_movements anywhere under server/ except tests;
  - the allow-list is pharmacy_stock_service, migrations.py (backfill, migration 35), helix_db.py (DDL), and the DELETE-only wipes in seed_helix and populate_helix_from_medgemma.

helix_service.py (grn-4)
- _atomic_dispense, _in_date_stock, get_inventory and both pre_flight functions delegate to the stock service.
- transition_order_status runs in db_session(immediate=True). Its in-body conn.commit() is removed, and the two re-reads run inside the block before it exits.
- Every dispense writes clinical_access 'helix_dispense_recorded' with db=conn: patient_id, order id, lot, quantity and movement id as string ids.
- receive_order is unchanged; it moves no stock.
- Substitution policy (R002) is not touched.

procurement_service.py (grn-20)
- Each write is split into a connection-taking core, _<name>_core(db, ..., domain), plus the existing public wrapper, which opens the immediate session with domain 'stores'. Stores behaviour and post-commit audit are unchanged.
- Every core that loads a document by id refuses a domain mismatch with code not_found (404).
- A GRN's domain is derived from its PO and never taken from the request.
- The pharmacy domain branch of post_goods_receipt never calls _insert_movement or updates inventory_items. It returns the posted lines for the caller.
- The cores take a 'today' argument: stores pass date.today() as now, and pharmacy passes site_today().
- Store master partition:
  - list_stores, get_store and upsert_store exclude rows with pharmacy_kind unless domain='pharmacy';
  - upsert_store refuses a code held by a pharmacy store;
  - record_stock_movement, issue_stock and the stores reports refuse or exclude pharmacy stores.
- _DOC_SERIES gains the pharmacy kinds.

Other new services
- pharmacy_purchasing_service.py (grn-7, grn-8, grn-22): opens db_session(immediate=True), calls the cores with domain 'pharmacy', calls pharmacy_stock_service, audits with db=conn in the same transaction, then stamps the document number after commit as procurement does.
- pharmacy_master_service.py (grn-5, grn-6): drug fields, classification with two-person downgrade, identity governance, pharmacy stores and adoption, par levels, vendors (through the vendor core) and drug licences.
- pharmacy_transfer_service.py (grn-11, grn-21).
- pharmacy_store_service.py (grn-10, grn-12, grn-15, grn-22).
- ndps_service.py (grn-13).

E. ROUTES
New router server/routes/pharmacy_store_routes.py at /api/pharmacy-store. Handlers are plain def. Each uses require_module plus one tier dependency built at import: _PS_READ, _PS_WRITE (read+write), _PS_APPROVE (read+approve) or _PS_NDPS (read+ndps).
- meta, overview.
- Masters: drugs, drugs/{id}/classification-requests, stores, par-levels, vendors (create and update through the shared vendor core, so the module works with ORB_PROCUREMENT=0), vendors/{code}/drug-licence.
- purchase-orders, plus submit, approve, issue, cancel and reorder-suggestions.
- goods-receipts, plus post and cancel.
- stock, lots, ledger (paged by seq), near-expiry, reorder, reconcile.
- lots/{id}/quarantine, recall and write-off; recall-trace; vendor-returns.
- transfers, plus dispatch, receive and cancel.
- indents, plus submit, decide and issue-plan.
- counts, plus submit and approve; adjustments; ward-returns, plus inspect.
- ndps/register, ndps/balances, ndps/variances, ndps/export.csv.
- Ward side, each gated on a ward_* permission plus department_scope: ward/stock, ward/transfers/awaiting, ward/transfers/{id}/receive, ward/indents, ward/returns.
- Errors: a wrong-domain or other-ward id is 404; a separation-of-duties refusal is 403; conflicts are 409.

Changes to existing routes:
- POST /api/helix/orders/{id}/transition gains optional dispense_quantity_units and lot_id, honoured only when the module is on (grn-14).
- main.py gains one include_router line.

F. PERMISSIONS (permissions.py; roles.py unchanged, so no users rebuild)
- New: pharmacy_store.read, pharmacy_store.write, pharmacy_store.approve, pharmacy_store.ndps, ward_stock.read, ward_stock.receive, ward_return.record, ward_indent.raise.
- helix.receive keeps its documented meaning: receipt of patient orders only.
- grn-2 grants admin pharmacy_store read, write and approve, mirroring admin's procurement grants from the 2026-08-18 desk split. The module is off by default, and GRN-R7 may change this. Nobody else gets anything.
- Pharmacist grants (read, write, ndps) and the pharmacist tab land in grn-19, blocked by GRN-R7 and GRN-R9.
- Nurse grants (ward_stock.read, ward_stock.receive, ward_indent.raise, ward_return.record) land with grn-21 and grn-15, blocked by GRN-R8 (W128).
- A test pins every defined-but-ungranted permission as deliberate.
- Separation rules, enforced in the service:
  - PO approver differs from the creator;
  - adjustment and write-off approver differs from the requester;
  - transfer receiver differs from the dispatcher;
  - count approver differs from the counter;
  - NDPS witness differs from the actor;
  - classification-downgrade approver differs from the requester.
- src/lib/roles.ts mirrors only what the UI gates on.

G. AUDIT
- Every pharmacy write audits through audit_service with db=conn inside the same immediate transaction as its stock movements.
- Document numbers are still stamped after commit. Allocation needs its own immediate session, and a number is not PHI. The audit row carries the document id as a string, and a stamping failure is logged and repairable as it is today.
- target_id is always str(). There is one row per document action; the ledger is the line record.
- 'clinical_access': helix_dispense_recorded (every dispense, grn-4), pharmacy_ward_return_recorded, pharmacy_ward_return_inspected.
- 'phi_access': pharmacy_recall_trace_viewed.

Both GRN-RS7 failure modes are built: 'block' runs the hook inside the dispense transaction; 'record' runs it in a SAVEPOINT, and on failure rolls back the register leg only, commits the dispense, and writes ndps_variances plus a 'security' audit row, all in the dispense transaction. The switch refuses to enable without ORB_PHARMACY_NDPS_ON_FAILURE. Reconciliation runs from the latest opening entry per drug and store. Register view, balances, variances, and an audited CSV export. Statutory form layouts stay with W170.

increments.tests: With the switch off, a narcotic dispense never calls the hook. With REGISTER=1 and no ON_FAILURE, the register stays off and an ERROR is logged. 'block': an injected hook failure rolls back the dispense. 'record': an injected failure commits the dispense, writes no register row, and writes one variance and one audit row. Every classified movement writes exactly one register row, and none on rollback. Register balance equals SUM(lots) per drug and store. Self-witness or a wrong PIN is refused and PIN lockout is respected. Live rows survive a reseed; non_production rows are cleared. Erasure and retention review skip live register rows. The export is audited.

increments.description: With the module on, the 'dispensed' transition accepts dispense_quantity_units (default 1, bounded by a site maximum) and an optional lot_id. The lot must be dispensable AND its medication_id must equal COALESCE(substitute_medication_id, medication_id), checked inside the immediate transaction; otherwise 422 lot_wrong_drug. A lot without enough quantity returns 409 and is never silently split. The quantity and lot go into helix_dispense_recorded. HelixOrderReviewModal shows quantity and a lot picker only with the module on. Starts after R024 lands.
increments.tests: Flag off: the new fields are ignored and behaviour is identical. Flag on: a lot of another drug, or of the prescribed drug when a substitute is set, gets 422. An expired, quarantined or ward lot is refused. The quantity is bounded. The drug-safety gate still screens the effective drug. The audit row carries the quantity and lot in the same transaction.

Nurse recording (ward_return.record with department_scope, DeliveriesSheet action) is granted only after GRN-R8. The return cannot exceed units dispensed minus units already returned. Units land in returns_quarantine as pending_inspection and are never dispensable. Inspection: write-off now; restock to the original lot only after GRN-RS3. clinical_access audit in the same transaction. Exposes a credit candidate for grn-16. NDPS returns go to the register when it is enabled.
increments.tests: Over-return is refused. Returned units are excluded from every dispensable count. Restock is unavailable until ruled. The audit row commits with the return or neither commits. With patched nurse grants, another ward's order gets 404.

The description names the dispensed drug. A ward return is a separate credit candidate keyed helix-return:<return id>, never a reuse of helix:<order>. Coordinate with the billing owner.

A lot with no MRP and no tariff skips with 'rate_not_configured', never 0. A replay does not double-charge. Flag off: candidates are unchanged.

product_rulings.question: GRN-RS1: Who may add a drug to the formulary, or change a drug's clinical identity (generic name, strength, form)? generic_name drives allergy and interaction screening.
product_rulings.options: (a) Any pharmacist alone, audited. (b) A pharmacist creates a draft; a second pharmacist or the medical lead confirms before it can be ordered; identity edits on rows with orders or stock are refused (retire and replace). (c) Only by import from a licensed knowledge base.
product_rulings.recommendation: (b), with the class preview shown before save. Held for Samuel.

product_rulings.question: GRN-RS2: Can a quarantined batch be released back to dispensable stock, and by whom? Are recalled or NSQ batches ever releasable?
product_rulings.options: (a) Any pharmacist with a reason. (b) A different pharmacist from the one who quarantined, with a reason, audited; recalled and NSQ are terminal. (c) Never.
product_rulings.recommendation: (b). Held for Samuel.

product_rulings.question: GRN-RS3: May medicines returned from a ward re-enter dispensable stock?
product_rulings.options: (a) Any in-date return. (b) Only sealed, in-date, non-cold-chain, non-NDPS unit packs after pharmacist inspection. (c) Never.
product_rulings.recommendation: (b). Held for Samuel.

product_rulings.question: GRN-RS4: Should a batch be dispensed when it expires within days, possibly before the supply runs out?
product_rulings.options: (a) Refuse within N days. (b) Warn and record a reason. (c) As today.
product_rulings.recommendation: (b), N a site setting defaulting to 30 days, until W117 gives a supply end date. Not built by this epic until ruled.

product_rulings.question: GRN-RS5: Which drugs may be held as ward imprest or crash-cart stock, and does administration from ward stock still need an active eMAR order?
product_rulings.options: (a) Any formulary drug. (b) A per-store list approved by pharmacy and the medical lead; concentrated electrolytes and site-listed high-alert drugs barred unless named; eMAR order still required. (c) No ward stock in v1.
product_rulings.recommendation: (b), starting the barred list from drug_safety_service's ISMP set. ORB_PHARMACY_WARD_STOCK stays off until ruled. Held for Samuel.

product_rulings.question: GRN-RS6: How is expiry entered at GRN, given that a typo can make an expired batch dispensable?
product_rulings.options: (a) GS1 scan only. (b) Typed twice and compared, plus scan when available. (c) Typed once.
product_rulings.recommendation: (b) now, (a) when scanners exist. Held for Samuel.

product_rulings.question: GRN-RS7 (new): When the NDPS register write fails, or would leave a negative balance, during a dispense of a controlled drug, what happens to the dispense?
product_rulings.options: (a) Block the dispense until the register is fixed. (b) Dispense; roll back only the register leg; record an NDPS variance and a security audit row; show it on the NDPS screen for same-day reconciliation. (c) As (b), and also block further NDPS dispenses of that drug in that store until it is reconciled.
product_rulings.recommendation: (b), so a bookkeeping fault never withholds analgesia while the variance is still captured in the same transaction. Both modes are built; the register cannot be enabled until this is ruled. Held for Samuel.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R7: Who holds the pharmacy-store permissions? Should a storekeeper role exist?
product_rulings.options: Pharmacist read, write and ndps; admin read and approve (or read, write and approve, mirroring procurement, as grn-2 grants in the interim); no grants at all until ruled. A storekeeper role needs a users-table rebuild.
product_rulings.recommendation: Pharmacist read, write and ndps; admin read and approve, dropping write after this ruling; no new role in v1.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R8 (W128): May nurses raise ward indents, see their ward's stock, receive ward transfers and record returns?
product_rulings.options: (a) Yes, through new ward_stock.read, ward_stock.receive, ward_indent.raise and ward_return.record grants, department-scoped; helix.receive unchanged. (b) The pharmacist does it on the ward's behalf. (c) Paper.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R9: May the pharmacist have a Pharmacy Store tab that shows purchase values, breaking the 'no money screen on a clinical rail' pin?
product_rulings.options: (a) Yes, as a pinned pharmacy-desk exception. (b) Stock views inside Helix only; money views admin-only.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). The pharmacist already holds procurement.write through the API.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R10: Must a vendor have a valid drug licence on file before a pharmacy PO or GRN?
product_rulings.options: Refuse; warn; ignore.
product_rulings.recommendation: Refuse, and warn 30 days before expiry.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R11: Separate number series for pharmacy documents?
product_rulings.options: Shared PO-/GRN- series, or PHPO/PHGRN/PHIND/PHTRF/PHVR/PHRET/PHCNT.
product_rulings.recommendation: Separate, configured by the site before first use.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R12: Drug costing and billing price.
product_rulings.options: Cost: lot landed cost spread over paid plus free units, or weighted average. Bill: batch MRP per unit, or tariff.
product_rulings.recommendation: Lot cost; bill the dispensed drug at batch MRP, with the tariff only where no MRP exists. Coordinate with the billing owner.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R13: Who decides dispense quantity until W117 exists?
product_rulings.options: The pharmacist enters it (default 1, site maximum), or it is computed from dose text.
product_rulings.recommendation: Pharmacist-entered and bounded.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R14: NDPS controls: where narcotics are dispensed from, who may witness, what a variance triggers, and whether seeds may hold NDPS stock.
product_rulings.options: Dispensing point: directly from the vault, or from a daily cabinet replenished by witnessed transfer. Witness: a second pharmacist, or also a registered nurse or doctor for ward wastage. Variance: report only, or also draft a NABH incident.
product_rulings.recommendation: Vault-only receipt. Dispense directly from the vault in v1, with the cabinet option available through transfers. Second-user PIN witness. Every variance drafts an incident. No NDPS stock in seeds. Confirm form layouts with W170.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R15: How is ward stock consumption accounted before eMAR links to the drug master?
product_rulings.options: Periodic count and top-up, or wait for automatic decrement.
product_rulings.recommendation: Count-based top-up now; grn-17 after the mos epic, never blocking a dose.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R16: Near-expiry window, alert delivery and minimum shelf life at receipt.
product_rulings.options: 60, 90 or 180 days; screen only or a Relay digest; minimum shelf life none, 90 days or a site value.
product_rulings.recommendation: 90 days, screen only, refuse receipts with under 90 days left unless approve tier overrides.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R17: Satellite pharmacies as dispensing points in v1?
product_rulings.options: One dispensing pharmacy with sub-stores, or several with routing.
product_rulings.recommendation: One per site in v1.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R18: May a drug with no schedule or NDPS classification be purchased or received?
product_rulings.options: Refuse, or treat unclassified as none.
product_rulings.recommendation: Refuse. Classification never gates a dispense of existing stock.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R19: Should the drug ledger be append-only by trigger?
product_rulings.options: Triggers on the ledger, or a single writer plus reconciliation and audit, with triggers on the NDPS register only.
product_rulings.recommendation: The latter. Ledger rows reference patient orders and are wiped on reseed.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R20 (new): Who may downgrade a drug's NDPS or schedule classification?
product_rulings.options: (a) Any holder of the write tier. (b) A request plus approval by a different approve-tier user, refused while vault stock exists. (c) Only the pharmacist-in-charge.
product_rulings.recommendation: (b). An upgrade applies at once, because it only adds control.

issues.issue: CHECK enums added by ALTER ADD COLUMN to FK-parent tables can never be changed. In the live schema, helix_inventory_lots is the declared FK parent of helix_stock_movements.lot_id. helix_medication_master is the parent of lots, movements and orders (both substitute_medication_id and medication_id). Changing a CHECK means rebuilding the table, and an FK-parent rebuild is impossible inside the migration transaction (memory note: both pragmas are no-ops). The enums are therefore fixed forever: lot status, drug_schedule, ndps_category, storage_condition. GRN-RS2 already names an NSQ state that the status enum lacks, and ruling outcomes such as 'destroyed' or 'expired', or schedules such as C/C1, would need the impossible rebuild.

issues.issue: The stores routes can still post drugs into the stores ledger, the second-ledger failure the design names as its top risk. Checked against the code on 3 Oct 2026: git baseline cafe363 plus uncommitted work in progress. The highest migration is 47 (vitals_carried_from), at server/migrations.py:5446-5495.

1. TWO STOCK SYSTEMS, BY DESIGN.
- Procurement owns non-pharmacy stock: vendors, stores, inventory_items, indents, indent_lines, purchase_orders, purchase_order_lines, goods_receipts, goods_receipt_lines and stock_movements (migration 20, migrations.py:2287-2552). By rule these tables have no foreign keys (migrations.py:1771).
- The drug boundary is enforced twice:
  - a database CHECK, `inventory_items.is_pharmacy ... CHECK (is_pharmacy = 0)` (migrations.py:2357);
  - `_helix_catalogue_match`, which refuses any stores item that matches the Helix formulary (procurement_service.py:823-875, 878-922; F103).
- Procurement's document machinery is mature and can be reused for drugs:
  - state machines held as data (procurement_service.py:216-243);
  - a draft-then-post GRN with idempotency key, over-receipt guard, refusal of expired stock on receipt, and PO status derived from the lines (procurement_service.py:1642-1956);
  - GST and paise arithmetic through services/money.py (compute_line :497, compute_invoice :594);
  - document numbers stamped after commit (procurement_service.py:397-452).
- The routes sit behind ORB_PROCUREMENT, which defaults ON (procurement_routes.py:76-96).
- There are three permission tiers (procurement_routes.py:106-108). The pharmacist holds procurement.read and write; admin holds all three.
- Every procurement write is audited under 'security' AFTER the service has committed (procurement_routes.py:133-157).

2. HELIX OWNS DRUGS BUT HAS NO STORE.
- helix_medication_master has five columns: id, name, generic_name, form, strength (helix_db.py:9-15). It has no pack size, HSN, GST, MRP, schedule, NDPS class or reorder level.
- The only API is read-only: GET /api/helix/catalog (helix_routes.py:16-19). Rows come only from scripts (scripts/seed_helix.py:13-62, populate_helix_from_medgemma.py).
- helix_inventory_lots is a balance table (helix_db.py:18-24): lot_number, quantity as INTEGER dispense units, expiration_date. It has no location, status, cost, MRP, supplier or receipt link.
- helix_stock_movements (helix_db.py:60-68) holds lot_id, medication_id, order_id, quantity_change, reason and timestamp.
  - It has no movement type, store, actor, running balance or idempotency key.
  - It is written in exactly one place, the dispense (helix_service.py:792-797).
- Nothing reconciles lots.quantity against SUM(movements), and seeded lots have no opening movement.
- GET /api/helix/stock-movements returns everything unpaged and no screen uses it (helix_routes.py:36-39; W120).

3. DISPENSE (helix_service.py:740-798).
- Fixed this week: FEFO now picks over in-date lots only (F064; _IN_DATE_LOT_SQL at :728; the hospital's "today" comes from the site timezone at :705-725). So the coverage map's "expired lots dispense first" no longer holds.
- Still open:
  - It always decrements exactly 1 unit (:783).
  - It picks from any lot of the drug, regardless of location.
  - transition_order_status runs in a default db_session (:277). The lot SELECT therefore runs in autocommit and the UPDATE writes an absolute value (:785), so two concurrent dispenses from one lot can lose a decrement. database.py:1103-1125 documents this class of race.
  - The dispense writes helix_transitions but no audit_service row.
- The R024 work added insert_order(conn, ...) at helix_service.py:219-240 today.

4. HELIX TABLES ARE CREATED OUTSIDE THE MIGRATION RUNNER.
- main.py:322 runs init_db, which runs the migrations (database.py:1983-1984). init_helix_db runs later and non-fatally, at main.py:388-392.
- On a fresh database, any migration that touches a Helix table therefore finds no table and does nothing. That is why:
  - migration 35 checks sqlite_master first (migrations.py:4920-4930);
  - helix_db.HELIX_SCHEMA has to carry new columns by hand.
- _migrate_stock_movements still logs a misleading INFO line on a fresh boot (helix_db.py:151-167; W027).

5. SCREENS.
- Pharmacist rail: helix, pharmacy-verify, sage (shellConfig.tsx:882-886).
- HelixPanel has three views: Overview, Patient Board and Formulary (HelixPanel.tsx:12-18).
  - Formulary shows lots with the server's in_date verdict and highlights expiry within 90 days (HelixFormulary.tsx:28).
  - Every drug uses a fixed low-stock threshold of 30 (src/components/helix/stock.ts:22).
- No screen exists for drug GRN, indents, transfers, adjustments, the ledger, expiry or reorder.
- ProcurementPanel.tsx (1,958 lines) states the drug boundary in its header (:5-18). Its ReceiveForm creates and posts a GRN in one step (W158).
- Admin modules mount through the module machinery in shellConfig.tsx:
  - HOSPITAL_MODULE_IDS (:177-184);
  - the lazy panel glob (:202-229);
  - DEFAULT_MODULE_FLAGS, all true (:249-252).
- shellConfig.test.ts:257-330 pins two things:
  - all module flags default ON;
  - no clinical role, the pharmacist included, gets any module tab other than dietary.

6. CUSTODY AND BILLING.
- Ward receipt of patient-specific dispenses is built:
  - helix.receive is held by nurses only;
  - the dispenser cannot also receive (helix_service.py:605-700, helix_routes.py:329-382, migration 35).
- Billing takes one tariff-priced line per dispensed or delivered Helix order (billing_service.py:182-190, 847-873). MRP does not exist anywhere in the code.

7. FLAGS.
- Every admin module uses config._module_enabled (config.py:642-648). They default ON per the 2026-08-11 ruling.
- They are registered in HOSPITAL_MODULE_ENV and enabled_modules() (config.py:799-830) and published on /api/health (main.py:1216).
- There is no opt-in (default OFF) helper, and no Ward Record profile exists in code.

8. TRAPS THAT SHAPE THE DESIGN.
- (a) The reseed wipes two kinds of table (reset_db_and_seed.py:124-205):
  - any table with a patient_id column;
  - any table with a `<parent>_id` column that names a wiped table, when no foreign key is declared.
  So a new column named order_id or medication_id with no declared FK would get its table wiped on every reseed.
- (b) users is the FK parent of about 20 tables, so adding a role means a users-rebuild migration (roles.py:20-27, migrations.py:4697).
- (c) Audit:
  - audit_service can write inside the caller's transaction via db= (audit_service.py:296-301);
  - the fail-closed categories are security, clinical_access, phi_access, authentication and ai_inference (audit_service.py:43-45);
  - an integer target_id breaks the audit chain, so it must be passed as a string.
- (d) No code mentions NDPS or Schedule H1, apart from:
  - a retention row (migrations.py:1265);
  - procurement text that wrongly says Helix tracks schedule-H (procurement_service.py:915, ProcurementPanel.tsx:9).
- (e) The Sage formulary lexicon is loaded once, at boot (main.py:398-403).

A. SHAPE
- Reuse Procurement's vendor master, PO, GRN and indent documents, state machines, GST math and numbering for drugs by adding a `domain` column.
- Keep Helix as the only owner of drug stock.
- Make one new Helix-side service the single writer of lots and of the drug ledger.
- inventory_items.is_pharmacy CHECK (is_pharmacy = 0) stays. No drug ever enters inventory_items or stock_movements, so there is still exactly one ledger per physical drug.

B. FEATURE FLAG (off by default)
- Server:
  - Add config._module_opt_in(env) beside _module_enabled: unset, blank or anything other than 1/true/on/yes means OFF.
  - PHARMACY_STORE_ENABLED = _module_opt_in('ORB_PHARMACY_STORE').
  - Register 'pharmacy-store' in HOSPITAL_MODULE_ENV and enabled_modules(), so /api/health publishes it.
- Client:
  - Add 'pharmacy-store' to HospitalModuleId.
  - Add OPT_IN_MODULE_IDS, whose DEFAULT_MODULE_FLAGS entry is false, so first paint never shows the tab.
- When the flag is off:
  - every /api/pharmacy-store route answers 404 module_disabled (the procurement require_module pattern);
  - there is no tab;
  - the Helix transition ignores the new dispense fields;
  - Helix screens are unchanged.
- Migrations still run; they are additive and invisible.
- grn-4 behaves identically for legacy lots (store_id NULL, status 'available'), so Ward Record and the demos are unaffected.

C. DATA MODEL
Migration numbers are taken at merge, after 47; other epics in this wave will also take numbers.

M-a helix_tables_in_runner (grn-1)
- A frozen copy of today's six Helix CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements plus their indexes.
- After this, later migrations can ALTER Helix tables on fresh and existing databases alike.
- init_helix_db stays as an idempotent fallback.

M-b pharmacy_store_schema (grn-3)
- Only ALTER ADD COLUMN, new tables and partial indexes. No table rebuilds, so the FK-parent rebuild trap cannot apply. No new foreign keys (the migration 20 rule).

New columns on helix_medication_master:
- pack_size_units INTEGER, purchase_uom TEXT, dispense_unit TEXT, hsn_code TEXT, manufacturer TEXT.
- gst_rate_bp INTEGER (NULL means not configured).
- drug_schedule TEXT CHECK (NULL or none, G, H, H1, X).
- ndps_category TEXT CHECK (NULL or none, narcotic, psychotropic). NULL means unclassified; it is never read as 'none'.
- is_essential_narcotic INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.
- storage_condition TEXT CHECK (NULL or room, cold_chain, frozen).
- reorder_level_units, reorder_qty_units, lead_time_days INTEGER.
- is_active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, updated_by, updated_at.

New columns on helix_inventory_lots:
- store_id INTEGER. NULL means the dispensing pharmacy, which is today's meaning.
- status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'available' CHECK (available, quarantined, recalled, pending_inspection, written_off, returned_to_vendor).
- units_per_pack, mrp_pack_paise, unit_cost_paise INTEGER.
- mfg_date DATE, vendor_id INTEGER, goods_receipt_line_id INTEGER, received_at TEXT, created_at TEXT.
- Index on (medication_id, store_id, status, expiration_date).
- Partial UNIQUE on (medication_id, store_id, lot_number, expiration_date) WHERE store_id IS NOT NULL.

New columns on helix_stock_movements:
- movement_type TEXT CHECK (NULL or opening, receipt, dispense, ward_return, return_restock, transfer_out, transfer_in, adjustment, count_variance, expiry_write_off, damage_write_off, vendor_return, consumption, op_sale).
- store_id, balance_after_units, unit_cost_paise, reference_type, reference_id, actor_id, remarks.
- idempotency_key, with a partial UNIQUE index.
- occurred_at TEXT, written with clinical_time.utc_iso_now(). Readers order by occurred_at DESC, rowid DESC.

New columns on procurement tables:
- purchase_orders.domain, goods_receipts.domain and indents.domain: TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'stores' CHECK (stores, pharmacy).
- indents.indent_kind: TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'purchase' CHECK (purchase, issue).
- indents.issuing_store_id.
- helix_medication_id and units_per_pack on purchase_order_lines, goods_receipt_lines and indent_lines.
- goods_receipt_lines: free_quantity_milli INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, mrp_pack_paise, mfg_date, helix_lot_id.
- indent_lines: issued_quantity_milli.
- vendors: drug_licence_numbers, drug_licence_valid_to, ndps_licence_number.
- stores.pharmacy_kind TEXT CHECK (NULL or dispensing, sub_store, ward_imprest, crash_cart, ndps_vault, returns_quarantine), with a partial UNIQUE index that allows one 'dispensing' store (the multi-site epic relaxes this to one per site).

New tables:
- pharmacy_par_levels: store_id, helix_medication_id, par_units, reorder_level_units, max_units; UNIQUE (store_id, helix_medication_id).
- pharmacy_transfers: transfer_number, from_store_id, to_store_id, indent_id, status (draft, dispatched, received, partially_received, cancelled), dispatched_by/at, received_by/at, cancel_reason, idempotency_key UNIQUE.
- pharmacy_transfer_lines: pharmacy_transfer_id, line_no, indent_line_id, helix_medication_id, from_lot_id, to_lot_id, batch_no, expiry_date, quantity_units, received_units, discrepancy_reason.

- ndps_register: store_id, helix_medication_id, lot_id, batch_no, entry_type, signed quantity_units, balance_after_units per drug and store, counterparty_type, counterparty_ref, patient_id, helix_order_id, document_ref, actor_id, witness_id, occurred_at, remarks. - Use helix_order_id and helix_medication_id, never order_id or medication_id. The reseed sweep would read those as links to `orders` and `medications` and wipe the table on every reseed.

Document series (is_configured=0): PHPO, PHGRN, PHIND, PHTRF, PHVR, PHRET, PHCNT.

D. SERVICES

services/pharmacy_stock_service.py (new)
- The ONLY writer of helix_inventory_lots.quantity and helix_stock_movements.
- post_movement(conn, ...) runs inside the caller's immediate transaction; it never opens a nested session. It:
  - does a relative UPDATE quantity = quantity + ?, guarded against going negative;
  - inserts the movement with balance_after, idempotency and actor;
  - calls the NDPS hook.
- Also provides:
  - open_or_merge_lot;
  - pick_fefo_lot: dispensing store only, status 'available', in date, FEFO;
  - dispensable_units;

- An AST test enforces the single-writer rule; seed scripts are allow-listed.

- services/pharmacy_transfer_service.py: issue indents, FEFO issue plans, dispatch, and ward receipt with receiver different from dispatcher.

- Masters: drugs, stores, par-levels, vendors/{code}/drug-licence.

product_rulings.question: GRN-RS1: Who may add a drug to the formulary, or change a drug's clinical identity (generic name, strength, form)? generic_name drives allergy and interaction screening, and today rows come only from seed scripts.
product_rulings.options: (a) Any pharmacist alone, audited. (b) A pharmacist creates; a second pharmacist or the medical lead confirms before the row can be ordered. Identity edits on a row with orders or stock are refused: retire it and create a new row. (c) Only by import from a licensed knowledge base.
product_rulings.recommendation: (b). The screen must show which allergy and interaction classes the generic will map to before save.

product_rulings.question: GRN-RS2: Can a quarantined batch be released back to dispensable stock, and by whom? Are recalled or NSQ (not of standard quality) batches ever releasable?
product_rulings.options: (a) Any pharmacist, with a reason. (b) A different pharmacist from the one who quarantined, with a reason, audited; recalled and NSQ are terminal. (c) No release ever.

product_rulings.question: GRN-RS3: May medicines returned from a ward re-enter dispensable stock?
product_rulings.options: (a) Any in-date return. (b) Only sealed, in-date, non-cold-chain, non-NDPS unit packs after pharmacist inspection; everything else is written off or destroyed by process. (c) Never.

product_rulings.question: GRN-RS4: Should a batch be dispensed when it expires within days, possibly before the supply runs out?
product_rulings.options: (a) Refuse when expiry is within N days. (b) Warn the pharmacist and record a reason. (c) As today: any in-date lot.
product_rulings.recommendation: (b), with N as a site setting defaulting to 30 days, until dispense quantity is schedule-derived (W117). Then compare against the supply end date.

product_rulings.question: GRN-RS5: Which drugs may be held as ward imprest or crash-cart stock? Does administration from ward stock still require an active eMAR order?
product_rulings.options: (a) Any formulary drug. (b) Only drugs on a per-store imprest list approved by pharmacy and the medical lead. Concentrated electrolytes (for example potassium chloride concentrate) and other site-listed high-alert drugs are barred unless named as an exception. eMAR order still required. (c) No ward stock in v1.
product_rulings.recommendation: (b). This design changes no administration gate.

product_rulings.question: GRN-RS6: How is expiry entered at GRN? A typo that makes an expired batch look in date would make it dispensable.
product_rulings.options: (a) GS1 barcode scan only. (b) Expiry typed twice and compared, plus scan when available. (c) Single typed entry.
product_rulings.recommendation: (b) now; (a) once scanners exist at the site.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R7: Who holds the new pharmacy-store permissions? Should a 'storekeeper' role be added?
product_rulings.options: Pharmacist read, write and ndps; admin read and approve; separation rules (approver is never the raiser) in the service. A storekeeper role needs a users-table rebuild migration.
product_rulings.recommendation: As listed. No new role in v1; a site that wants a pharmacist-in-charge approver gets an explicit grant.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R8 (W128): May nurses raise ward indents to pharmacy and see their own ward's stock?
product_rulings.options: (a) Yes: ward_indent.raise plus a ward stock view, department-scoped, with receipt via helix.receive. (b) Pharmacist raises on the ward's behalf. (c) Paper.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R9: The shell rule keeps every non-dietary module (money screens) off clinical rails. Should the pharmacist get a Pharmacy Store tab that shows purchase values?
product_rulings.options: (a) Yes, as a pinned pharmacy-desk exception. (b) Pharmacist gets stock views inside Helix only; money views stay admin-only.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). The pharmacist already holds procurement.read and write through the API, and drug purchasing is pharmacy work.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R10: Must a vendor have a valid drug licence on file before a pharmacy PO or GRN?
product_rulings.options: Refuse; warn; ignore.
product_rulings.recommendation: Refuse for the pharmacy domain, and warn 30 days before licence expiry.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R11: Separate document number series for pharmacy POs, GRNs, indents, transfers and returns?
product_rulings.options: Shared PO-/GRN- series, or PHPO/PHGRN/PHIND/PHTRF/PHVR/PHRET/PHCNT.
product_rulings.recommendation: Separate series, configured by the site before first use.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R12: Costing and billing price for drugs.
product_rulings.options: Cost: lot landed cost including non-creditable GST spread over paid plus free units, or weighted average. Bill: batch MRP per unit, or tariff price list.
product_rulings.recommendation: Lot cost; bill at batch MRP (a DPCO ceiling), with the tariff only where no MRP exists. Coordinate with the billing owner.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R13: Who decides dispense quantity until the authored administration schedule (W117) exists?
product_rulings.options: Pharmacist enters it (default 1, site maximum); or computed from dose and frequency text.
product_rulings.recommendation: Pharmacist-entered and bounded. Computed quantity comes with the single medication-order store.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R14: NDPS controls: vault-only receipt, who may witness, and what a variance triggers. May demo seeds contain NDPS stock?
product_rulings.options: Witness by a second pharmacist; or any registered nurse or doctor for ward wastage. Variance: report only, or auto-draft a NABH incident.
product_rulings.recommendation: Vault-only receipt. Second-user PIN witness: pharmacist plus admin for vault adjustments, and a registered nurse or doctor for ward wastage. Every variance drafts an incident. No NDPS stock in seeds, because the register is append-only and survives reseeds. Confirm form layouts with the W170 owner.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R15: How is ward stock consumption accounted before eMAR doses link to the drug master?
product_rulings.options: Periodic count and top-up; or wait for automatic decrement on administration.
product_rulings.recommendation: Count-based top-up now; automatic decrement (grn-17) once the mos epic lands, never blocking a dose.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R16: Near-expiry window, alert delivery and minimum shelf life on receipt.
product_rulings.options: Window 60, 90 or 180 days. Alerts on screen only, or also a daily Relay digest. Minimum shelf life on receipt: none, 90 days, or a site value.
product_rulings.recommendation: 90 days; screen only first; refuse receipts with under 90 days left unless approve tier overrides.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R17: Satellite pharmacies (OT, ICU) as dispensing points in v1?
product_rulings.options: One dispensing pharmacy with satellites as sub-stores; or multiple dispensing stores with order routing.
product_rulings.recommendation: One dispensing pharmacy per site in v1. Routing belongs with the multi-site and medication-order epics.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R18: May a drug with no schedule or NDPS classification be purchased or received?
product_rulings.options: Refuse; or allow and treat unclassified as 'none'.
product_rulings.recommendation: Refuse. Unclassified is not 'none', or the NDPS hook could be bypassed by leaving the field blank.

product_rulings.question: GRN-R19: Should the drug stock ledger (helix_stock_movements) be append-only by trigger?
product_rulings.options: Triggers on the ledger; or integrity by single writer, reconciliation and audit, with triggers on the NDPS register only.
product_rulings.recommendation: The latter. Ledger rows reference patient orders, and triggers would collide with DPDP erasure and reseed.

risks: A second drug ledger is the failure the codebase warns about. inventory_items.is_pharmacy CHECK must stay, and pharmacy GRNs must never call procurement _insert_movement. Enforce with an AST test, not convention.
Helix tables live outside the migration runner until grn-1. Any Helix ALTER shipped before it no-ops on fresh databases.
The existing dispense has a lost-update race (autocommit read plus absolute UPDATE at helix_service.py:277/785). grn-4 fixes it. Until then, concurrent dispenses can undercount.
The reseed sweep wipes any table whose `<parent>_id` column names a wiped table. New columns must use helix_order_id and helix_medication_id, and test_reseed_orphans must cover the new tables.
The opening-balance backfill dates opening rows at migration time, so ledger history before the migration is incomplete by construction. The remark must say so rather than invent dates.

About ten tests and two seed scripts insert lots directly, bypassing the ledger. reconcile() will report mismatches on dev DBs until seed_helix is changed (grn-4) and test fixtures move to the service.
The NDPS register is append-only and keyed to patients. It survives reseeds and must be excluded from DPDP erasure, which needs coordination with the W168 legal-hold work.

Units: purchase packs versus integer dispense units. Liquids, partial ampoules and MRP-per-unit rounding need explicit rules. Pack size not configured must block receipt, not default to 1.
